advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the name-string SelectionStaleError check in run_pass with an isinstance test against the loaded reconcile_helpers.SelectionStaleError class (mirroring the RescheduleError arm).
evidence: The sibling RescheduleError/ReconcileLockLost arms use isinstance against a loaded class (__main__.py:467, 473), so this name-string match is inconsistent with the surrounding pattern.
reconcile.py already re-exports the class: `SelectionStaleError = _helpers.SelectionStaleError` (reconcile.py:66), so an isinstance check against the loaded reconcile/helpers class is available.
advisory.finding: run_pass classifies the stale-selection exit code by matching the exception class name string (type(exc).__name__ == "SelectionStaleError") rather than isinstance against the loaded class. A future rename of SelectionStaleError, or an unrelated exception coincidentally sharing the name, would silently mis-route: a rename would drop the exit-2 mapping (falling through to exit 1), and a namesake would wrongly produce exit 2.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider consolidating the duplicated _positive_int validator (or accept the CLI copy as a fast-fail and note the intentional duplication).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py adds `_positive_int` raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be a positive integer")`
advisory.finding: _positive_int is duplicated verbatim in src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py and src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/request.py. Both validate --max-changes as a positive int, so the CLI-side check is effectively redundant with the engine-side check, and the two copies can drift (e.g. one gets a clearer message).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the `sync` command line in bridge.txt and cli-reference.md to match the new argparse help ("Apply proposed Jira changes") instead of "Apply the staged Jira synchronization".
evidence: bridge.txt: `  sync      Apply the staged Jira synchronization`
cli-reference.md: `  sync      Apply the staged Jira synchronization`
_bridge_commands.py: `help="Apply proposed Jira changes.",` / `description="Apply proposed Jira changes.",`
Both files updated the group description ("Run staged Jira synchronization." → "Synchronize rebar tickets with Jira.") but left the `sync` command line describing "the staged Jira synchronization".
advisory.finding: The pinned bridge help (`bridge.txt`) and `cli-reference.md` still describe the `sync` command as "Apply the staged Jira synchronization", but the argparse definition in `_bridge_commands.py` was changed to "Apply proposed Jira changes." (and the group description to "Synchronize rebar tickets with Jira."). The `sync` command line was not updated to match.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the `sync` line in both `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` and `docs/cli-reference.md` to `  sync      Apply proposed Jira changes`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests for each request.py conflict guard (--mode+command, --max-changes without sync, --filter-local-ids on primary route, --only/--except without command) asserting exit/RequestError and message.
evidence: request.py:98 `raise RequestError("primary preview/sync commands cannot be combined with --mode")`
request.py:102 `raise RequestError("--max-changes is supported only by sync")`
request.py:104-105 `--filter-local-ids is available only on the legacy route`
search of tests for `normalize_request` / `cannot be combined with --mode` / `is supported only by sync` returns only source hits, no test hits
test_bridge_request_heldout.py covers preview/sync mode mapping, valid + invalid --max-changes, and unresolved selection, but none of the mutual-conflict guards
advisory.finding: The new request-normalizer conflict guards in request.py have no test coverage. normalize_request raises RequestError for four distinct invalid combinations (preview/sync + --mode; --max-changes without sync e.g. `preview --max-changes 5`; --filter-local-ids on the primary route; --only/--except without a preview/sync command), each returning exit 2, but no test exercises these branches. They are reachable via direct `python -m rebar_reconciler ...` invocation (used by _dc_support.run_bridge and the pressure-test scripts), so a regression that dropped or mis-mapped a guard would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized test invoking `request.normalize_request(argv, mode_mod)` (or `main([...])`) for each invalid combination and assert RequestError / exit code 2 with the specific message.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving run_pass/main so ensure_selection_current raises SelectionStaleError mid-pass, asserting exit code 2 and the ERROR message on stderr.
evidence: test_bridge_selection_scope_heldout.py:119 `pytest.raises(ValueError, match="vanished")` exercises reconcile_once, not run_pass/main exit code
search for `SelectionStaleError` shows only source usages plus the one reconcile-level test match; no test asserts the exit-2 boundary
advisory.finding: The SelectionStaleError -> exit-code-2 classification in run_pass/main is untested at the process boundary. reconcile_helpers.ensure_selection_current raising the stale error is exercised only through reconcile_once (test_bridge_selection_scope_heldout.py asserts `pytest.raises(ValueError, match="vanished")`), but the fail-closed contract that __main__ translates this specific error into exit code 2 (distinct from the generic exit 1) — via the fragile `type(exc).__name__ == "SelectionStaleError"` comparison — has no test.
advisory.suggested_fix: In an orchestrate heldout test, patch reconcile_once (or the local-ticket read) so ensure_selection_current raises SelectionStaleError, invoke main([...]) with a resolvable selection, and assert rc == 2 and 'stale' in stderr.
